outlook.statement: The Indian automobile industry recorded one of its strongest performances in FY 2025-26, achieving the highest ever sales across all vehicle categories. Similarly Indian railway continued to be the largest rail networks in the world and remains a key driver of India's infrastructure development. Amid the dynamic landscape of the automotive and rail sector, our Company continued its growth trajectory.

The Company remains agile, tracking geopolitical development and their evolving macro environment. In parallel, the Company is actively assessing the risk landscape and has put in place appropriate mitigation measures to strengthen resilience.

The investment segment faced some challenges related to fluctuations in interest rates, volatile stock market, currency depreciation and global uncertainties. However, performance of investment operations remains stable with a conservative approach towards deployment of funds, keeping capital protection in focus.
The working of Company's Joint venture viz. Compo Advics (India) Private Limited, has slightly improved with several steps taken towards change in product mix and cost reduction program.

Despite geo-political uncertainties and global slowdowns, the outlook for FY 2026-27 remains positive. India is expected to continue its growth trajectory supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals, infrastructure development, and government initiatives.

The long-term outlook for the Indian rail sector remains highly positive. Continued government investment, modernization initiatives, freight corridor expansion, indigenous manufacturing programs, and increasing passenger mobility are expected to drive sustained growth.

Industry stakeholders remain optimistic regarding FY 2026-27, although crude oil prices, commodity costs, exchange rate fluctuations, and geopolitical developments continue to require close monitoring.

The automotive industry is likely to maintain steady growth across vehicle categories, driven by domestic demand, exports, technological advancements, and policy support. Demand for the company's products used in segments like Commercial Vehicles, passenger cars, tractors, railway and industry should improve considerably. The company will remain part of this change with appropriate products and solutions for customers. The company will continue to put a thrust on new product development to meet the changed requirements of customers, provide better customer service and continue to work towards up-gradation of technology, improvement in quality, cost rationalisation, cash preservation, and digitalisation. Besides, the company will continue to aggressively pursue opportunities for new OEM approvals, improve market share in OE and aftermarket. The company will keep working with Indian railway and wagon manufacturers to develop superior friction material for its requirements.

The Company is exposed to the risk of price fluctuations of raw materials, which are proactively managed by forward booking of materials, inventory management and vendor development practices. With regard to foreign exchange risk, there is natural hedging of risk as our import and export generally remains at the same level.
